ratings.reviewer_notes: In a Kras G12D lung cancer model, alveolar macrophage glycolysis and glucose uptake were associated with impaired SOCS3 secretion, which was reversed by glycolysis inhibition. This supports a metabolic immune-suppression mechanism, but does not directly establish that KRAS mutation causes the macrophage metabolic shift.
Directly reviews how KRAS-driven metabolic reprogramming and autophagy converge with other pathways to cause immune evasion, particularly in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.

This review is specifically focused on immune suppression caused by oncogenic KRAS through metabolic reprogramming and discusses multiple metabolic pathways that alter immune-cell phenotypes and functions.
Establishes KRAS-to-immune-evasion signaling through ERK-dependent PD-L1 upregulation and T-cell apoptosis, but does not identify a metabolic pathway.

Directly identifies a KRASG12C-associated metabolic immune-evasion pathway in colorectal liver metastasis: AKR1B10 increases glycolysis and lactate, causing neutrophil histone lactylation, PD-L1 transcription, and immunosuppressive reprogramming.
Provides an informative RAS-mutant model in which extracellular lactate induces PD-L1 and activates MEK/ERK, but it concerns HRASG12V rather than KRAS.
Broad review of how KRAS shapes the colorectal tumor microenvironment; the abstract does not identify metabolic pathways connecting KRAS mutation to immune evasion.
Defines a relevant glycolysis-lactate-H3K18 lactylation-B7-H3 pathway that suppresses CD8 T-cell immunity, but the study does not connect this pathway to KRAS mutation.

Shows that oncogenic KRAS enables Th2-derived IL4/IL13 signaling through JAK1-STAT6-MYC to drive glycolysis in pancreatic cancer cells. It supplies a KRAS-linked metabolic pathway, but immune evasion is not directly demonstrated.
Reviews KRAS-driven immune-evasion programs and PD-L1-centered networks, offering relevant mechanistic context, but the abstract does not specifically identify metabolic pathways.
